#8607. What the Full Moon in Gemini Means for You

There are breakthroughs, large and small, awaiting you on the full Moon in Gemini. Insights that have the power to change everything can arrive in an instant. A sentence you have repeated to yourself for years might suddenly sound false. A thought that once felt like a fact might reveal itself as a fear. You might hear yourself say something about your life and realize, in the middle of saying it, that you no longer believe it. It’s a powerful supermoon, one designed to help you release what no longer belongs to you.

The Moon reaches its fullest light on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, at 6:54 am PT.

Gemini is the sign of the twins, ruled by the planet Mercury and the element of air. It moves quickly, influencing our intellect and communication and touching our minds, our nervous systems, our voices, and the way we take in and share information. Gemini is the part of us that asks questions, makes connections, strikes up a conversation with a stranger, and wants to know a little about everything. It is curiosity in motion.

The twins also represent duality. Gemini reminds us that we are complex, that we can hold two feelings at once, and that life is rarely black or white. There are shades of gray everywhere, and within that uncertainty exists endless possibility.

Gemini is the voice in your head that narrates your day. It names what is happening to you, decides what it means, and tells you what to expect next. This voice speaks to you more than any other person in your life. It is there when you wake up and when you fall asleep. It comments on your work, your relationships, and your decisions. It is the stories you live by. Most of the time, you do not even notice it is speaking. It feels less like a voice and more like the truth.

But it is a voice. And a voice can change.

Think about where your inner voice came from. Some of it is yours, formed through your own experience and your own knowing. Some of it was inherited. A parent’s worry. A teacher’s doubt. A sentence someone said to you once, at the wrong moment, that you have been repeating to yourself ever since. Some of it came from society, from every message that told you who you were supposed to be and how much you were allowed to want. Over the years, all of these voices blended into one, and you started to call it you.

The words you use about yourself become the life you live. If your inner voice tells you something is not possible, you stop reaching for it. You do not apply, you do not ask, you do not try, and the life that follows proves the voice right. But when the voice changes, the reaching changes. And when the reaching changes, the life changes. A new inner voice is how you begin to believe what is possible.

There is science behind this. Research on moments of insight, those sudden aha experiences, shows that they tend to arrive when we’re in a less-anxious state of mind rather than straining for an answer. The brain makes surprising connections when we stop gripping the problem. This full Moon asks you to slow down, breathe, and loosen your hold on the old voice before reaching for the new one. The breakthrough comes more easily when you make space for it.

Gemini is also one of the most social signs of the zodiac, and that is part of the medicine. Sometimes the new voice arrives through someone else. A friend reflects you back to yourself in a way you never considered. A stranger says the exact sentence you needed. A line in a book or a song lands differently than it ever has before. Be open to these messages. Stay curious. Talk to people. Listen more than usual. The universe often delivers our breakthroughs through the voices of others.

On the full Moon in Gemini, let yourself be curious about your own mind. Listen to the voice in your head as if you were hearing it for the first time. Notice what it says. Notice whose voice it sounds like. And then notice the quieter voice underneath, the one that has always believed in you. That is the voice that is ready to rise.

As the Moon in Gemini finds itself opposite the Sun in Sagittarius, we can experience the illumination of both signs. Of all the opposing signs of the zodiac, Gemini and Sagittarius are the most alike. Both are in search of truth. Both follow their curiosity wherever it leads. Both love to learn, explore, and share what they discover. Gemini occupies the third house of communication and the immediate world around us. Sagittarius occupies the ninth house of truth, philosophy, and the wider world. Together they form the axis of the mind.

Gemini sees the details. Sagittarius sees the big picture. Gemini collects the individual pieces of information. Sagittarius weaves them into meaning. Gemini asks what is happening. Sagittarius asks why. Together they give us a complete view of how we think.

This year, there is another way to see this axis. Gemini is the voice. Sagittarius is the belief.

Your beliefs are the things you hold to be true about life, about yourself, and about what is possible. They shape everything. But beliefs are not built in a single day. They are built, sentence by sentence, from the words you hear and repeat. Every time your inner voice says something, it adds to a belief. Say “things never work out for me” enough times and it becomes a philosophy. Say “something good is always on its way” enough times and that becomes a philosophy, too.

This is the gift of the Gemini and Sagittarius opposition on this full Moon. When the voice changes, the belief follows. As you release the old voice and let the new one rise, you are not only changing your thoughts. You are rebuilding what you believe is possible for your life. And Sagittarius, ruled by Jupiter, the planet of expansion, gives that belief room to become as big as your life is meant to be.

With the full Moon, we have the opportunity to release the lower vibrations of these signs and integrate the higher ones.

Gemini’s lower vibration shows up as scattered thinking and division. In this frequency, the mind races. We jump from thought to thought without landing anywhere. We talk more than we listen. We overshadow other people’s truth to prove our own knowledge. We get lost in the details, in the noise, in the endless information coming at us, and we lose the thread of what we actually feel. We might repeat the same anxious story over and over, and each time it gets louder. Gemini’s low side can also look like gossip, overthinking, and indecision, where two voices inside us argue and neither one wins.

If you find yourself in the lower vibration of Gemini, slow down. Take a long, slow breath and bring yourself back into your body. Spend more time listening than talking. When you notice the mind racing, ask yourself one simple question. What is true right now? Then let the rest go quiet.

Sagittarius has a lower vibration, too. It looks like certainty. In this frequency, we believe we already have all the answers. We become self righteous about our views and close ourselves off to anything that challenges them. We forget that everyone has something to teach us. Sagittarius’s low side can also show up as restlessness and always chasing the next horizon instead of arriving where we are. Sometimes it looks like the opposite of faith. It can be a belief that life is working against us, held just as tightly as any other philosophy.

If you find yourself in the lower vibration of Sagittarius, get curious about a perspective that is different from yours. Ask yourself which of your beliefs you chose and which you simply inherited. Release your need to be right. This is your permission to change your mind about your own life.

When we align with the higher vibrations of both signs, Gemini gives us a voice that is curious, open, and kind. Sagittarius gives us a belief that is expansive and full of faith. They create someone who speaks to themselves like a trusted friend, who believes in what is possible, and who is always willing to learn. We understand the details of what is needed to create our intentions, and we hold the vision of where we are headed.

The highest merger of these energies teaches us that there is no you or me. There is only us. Every voice we hear, every story we are told, every conversation we have is part of one great exchange. When we open our minds to one another, the messages we need find us at just the right time.

Each full Moon carries its own astrological fingerprint, with other cosmic bodies forming their own conversations on that day. These conversations are called aspects, and they add layers of meaning to the full Moon. Some create tension. Others create flow. Together they shape the emotional landscape you are working with. On the full Moon in Gemini, the story of the aspects is one of support.

The entire axis of this full Moon is charged with Uranus. The Moon reaches its fullest light in Gemini. Just over one degree away sits Uranus. The Moon and Uranus are conjunct, which means they share the same part of the sky and blend their energies together. The next afternoon, the Sun reaches its exact opposition to Uranus.

Uranus is the planet of awakening. It rules sudden insight, liberation, innovation, and the unexpected. It is the flash of lightning that lights up an entire landscape in an instant, revealing what was there all along. Uranus breaks patterns. It frees us from whatever has become too small, too rigid, or too old for who we are becoming. Its gifts often arrive quickly, and sometimes they are a surprise. But they always move us toward more liberation and more truth.

Uranus entered Gemini on April 26, 2026, the first time it was in this sign since the 1940s. Out in the world, Uranus in Gemini is sparking a revolution in communication, technology, and the way we learn and share information. Within each of us, it is sparking a revolution in the way we speak to ourselves.

Right now, Uranus is retrograde. It stationed retrograde on September 10, 2026, in Gemini and will station direct on February 8th, 2027, in Gemini. When a planet is retrograde, its energy turns inward. So the breakthrough of this full Moon is not about what you say out loud to the world. It is about what you say to yourself. With Uranus sitting beside it, Gemini’s speed meets Uranus’s suddenness, and that combination is powerful.

This full Moon in Gemini also a Supermoon. A Supermoon happens when the Moon reaches its fullest light near perigee, which is the closest point to the Earth in its orbit. It appears larger and brighter than usual as it rises. Energetically, a Supermoon amplifies everything influenced by the full Moon. Emotions feel bigger. Insights land with more force. Release runs deeper. With Uranus sitting right beside the Moon, the breakthrough with your inner voice is turned all the way up.

This year, the Sun also forms a trine to Neptune in Aries, a harmonious connection between our sense of self and our dreams. Neptune adds faith, vision, and imagination to this opposition. It helps Sagittarius believe in something bigger than what it can see. It softens the edges of the old voice and makes room for the dream underneath it. As you work with the full Moon in Gemini, let yourself imagine. Let yourself dream bigger than feels reasonable. Neptune is helping you see a life your old voice never had words for.

There is a voice that speaks to you more than any other. It is with you in the shower and in the car, in meetings and in quiet moments, when you look in the mirror and when you lie awake at night. It is the voice in your own head. Most of us never stop to question it. We assume that what it says is simply true.

But this voice was shaped over a lifetime, by experiences, by people, by pain, and by the world around us. Some of what it says is wise. Some of it is love. And some of it is old, outdated, and borrowed from people who did not know who you would become.

This full Moon in Gemini, with Uranus sitting beside it, is your opportunity to hear that voice clearly and to choose a new one. A voice that believes in you. A voice that can carry you into 2027 and help you see what is possible for your life.

The changes this full Moon brings are meant to free you, not to shake you apart. Let the old voice go. Listen for the new one. It has been waiting for you. So step outside on the evening of the full Moon in Gemini and look up as it rises. Let the size of that Moon remind you how big your life is allowed to be.

Learn more about the full Moon in Taurus, including additional astrological insights and journaling prompts, in the Gemini Full Moon Workbook, from which the above is excerpted.

#8606. The Best Compact Rowing Machines for Small Spaces in 2025

A smaller footprint doesn’t mean you have to miss out. Here are the best compact rowing machines for a top-notch workout.

Written by Stephen Sheehan, CPT × The Expert Panel is a network of specialized health and fitness professionals who help ensure we present the most accurate information to our readers. This includes physicians, certified trainers, elite-level coaches, and more. Learn more about our experts. expert-verified Amanda Dvorak, ISSA-CPT, ISSA-CNC Last updated on Mar 4, 2025

expert-verified Amanda Dvorak, ISSA-CPT, ISSA-CNC

If you’re limited on space, don’t let the length of a rowing machine deter you. While there are many great rowing machines on the market, there are also some awesome compact alternatives that offer all the same tech features you’ll find in other cardio machines.

During our search for the best compact rowing machine, we found an array of excellent standalone options and options that fit in well with other top-rated home gym equipment. We considered the overall footprint and other key features, and scoured the reviews to see what users had to say about each product. Below is our list of the best compact home rowing machines available.

The rowing machines included in this list were carefully selected based on what most users would want out of a rowing machine, keeping in mind that they needed to have a smaller footprint and folding or upright storage options. We evaluated each choice based on size, portability, cost, high-tech features, versatility, and durability. We also scoured the reviews to see what users had to say about each rowing machine.

On the Hydrow website, the Hydrow Wave is rated 4.6/5 stars with over 9,000 reviews at the time of writing. It’s the brand’s compact, budget-friendly option for those who want to elevate their at-home workout routine. The length is just 80 inches, which is the shortest on this list, and the overall size is 30 percent shorter than the original Hydrow Rower. You cannot fold it, but there is the option to store it upright using The Hydrow Wave Vertical Anchor. This is a wall-mounted strap that holds the rower upright. It costs an additional $190, which is a bit on the pricey side.

The frame is made of aluminum and steel. It has a flat anthracite polymer body, which is a durable and lightweight material. The handle has an ergonomic design for a low-stress grip, and the strap is made from water- and rot-resistant polyester webbing. It also has a patented electromagnetic drag system that mimics the experience of rowing on open water.

Overall, the reviews on the Hydrow website are positive, and many mention how quiet the machine is and how much they like the small footprint. One review says, “The machine is such great quality. It’s quiet and sleek looking.” The critical reviews make up 3 percent of the overall reviews and state issues like non-working parts being delivered. However, Hydrow has responded to each review to resolve any issues.

The NordicTrack RW700 has a 10-inch HD touchscreen you can tilt and pivot to follow along with an iFIT workout led by your favorite trainer on or off the rower. An iFIT subscription is $39 per month, and you’ll have access to live and on-demand classes. Membership to the fitness app is not required to use the rower; however, you won’t have access to trainer-led classes without it.

A trainer-led rowing workout gives you the option to row on the open water for a more scenic experience, and there are also studio sessions. The resistance is adjusted automatically among 26 resistance levels during each class, so you don’t need to worry about stopping to make changes. The oversized foot pedals have adjustable nylon foot straps with quick release, which is excellent for those who want to incorporate movements off the rower into their workout.

The rail is 87 inches long and made from durable steel. It has an inertia-enhanced flywheel, so it should maintain a smooth rotation. If you have a shared space, the NordicTrack RW700 rower has a magnetic resistance system that creates tension against the flywheel without touching, making it a quieter option. After your workout, this magnetic rowing machine can be moved using the front wheels, but it can’t be folded.

The flywheel has been designed to maintain inertia and rotate smoothly, and the steel rail is oversized to help keep you stable. The large, pivoting foot pedals with adjustable nylon straps keep your feet in place, and the seat is molded with comfort in mind.

If you like to incorporate other movements into your rowing workout or train off of the rower, the Echelon Row-s has a 22-inch HD touchscreen that can be flipped 180 degrees. While an Echelon Fit subscription is not required, the extra $35/month workout app gives you access to over 40 live classes and more than 1,000 on-demand workouts from its library, including rowing, biking, running, and functional training classes.

The ergonomic design of the seat and the ability to adjust the foot platforms to a comfortable position help you maintain proper posture and alignment. If you’re short on space, the length goes from 84 inches long to just 41 inches long when folded. On the Echelon website, this rower is rated 4.6/5 stars. “The machine looks great, operates very quietly, and gives a great workout no matter your level,” says reviewer Brett P.

Dimensions: 87.02" L x 22.0" W x 47.24" H

Storage: Folds in half for vertical storage

Available programming: Live and on-demand workouts, scenic rows

The NordicTrack RW600 balances great tech features and an accessible price, making it a great value. The 10-inch screen is an excellent option for those who want to take instructor-led classes using an iFIT membership. NordicTrack’s patented Silent Magnetic Resistance can be adjusted up to 26 levels automatically in an iFIT class or manually as needed.

The pivoting foot pedals are oversized, and the nylon straps keep your feet secure. The handlebar has a soft grip, and the molded seat is designed to help you feel comfortable. When your workout is finished, the NordicTrack RW600 can be folded and stored out of the way.

What factors should you consider before you pull the trigger on a rower? Here’s what we’d recommend you take into account as you ponder your purchase decision:

Once you’ve decided on your rower location, it’s a good idea to measure the length, width, and height of your space to determine what size machine works best. You’ll want to measure height to see if you have enough clearance for rowers to be stored upright.

After measuring, think about how much you’re willing to spend. Take into consideration any additional costs such as a monthly subscription. Some rowers also have add-ons for purchase, such as a lumbar support system or seat upgrade.

Ask yourself: How many levels of resistance do I need? Am I looking for an HD touchscreen with trainer-led classes or do I prefer a more simplistic display? Other features such as a magnetic resistance system may be important if you’re in a shared space and need a quieter machine. The rower’s maximum height and/or weight capacity may also play a role in your decision as well.

Rowing allows you to implement low-impact, cardio-based training, and you can adjust the resistance for a strength-focused session. It’s a full-body workout that uses 86 percent of your muscles. With each stroke, you’re using your core and legs for the initial pull and finishing the rowing movement by using your upper body. Since you’re in a seated position, there’s less pressure on your knee and ankle joints.

Getting all four types of exercise (endurance, strength, balance, and flexibility) has benefits, according to The National Institute of Health (NIH). A rowing machine can be utilized for two types: endurance and strength. Many rowing machines have built-in programs or subscriptions that offer classes geared toward building strength and endurance.

Rowing is a great way to build strength and endurance while working various muscle groups. There are choices to suit a variety of budgets with different storage options and sizes. Figuring out how much space you have, your price range and the features you’d like will help you choose the best compact rowing machine for you.

The machines on this list range from just over $700 to around $2,000. You can find a rower in your price range, but if you opt for a rower under, say, $200, you may be compromising quality.

Typically, rowing machine length ranges between six to nine feet with more compact options at six or seven feet long.

The level of resistance that’s best for you depends on your fitness level, experience, and goals. Overall, you don’t want your workout to be too easy or so challenging you don’t accomplish the goal of your training session.

Compact rowing machines usually have air or magnetic resistance, and some options implement both.

Stephen is an ISSA-certified personal trainer and nutritionist with an immense passion for health and fitness. A two-time University of Florida graduate and longtime rugby player, he brings more than a decade of strength training experience, plus a diverse writing and editing background. When he’s not creating content or hitting the gym, he enjoys traveling, cooking, and attending music festivals around the world.

The Breaking Muscle newsletter is everything you need to know about strength in a 3 minute read.

Breaking Muscle is the fitness world’s preeminent destination for timely, high-quality information on exercise, fitness, health, and nutrition. Our audience encompasses the entire spectrum of the fitness community: consumers, aficionados, fitness professionals, and business owners. We seek to inform, educate and advocate for this community.

#8605. The Best Asics Running Shoes Deliver Cushion, Stability, and Speed—Here Are Our Editors’ Top Picks

On this list: incredibly bouncy trainers, plush cushioned shoes, and zippy racers by the “tiger stripes” brand.

We earn a commission for products purchased through some links in this article. Why Trust Us?

Editor’s Note, November 23, 2026: Black Friday discounts are in full swing. Asics legacies, the Gel-Cumulus 28 and Gel Nimbus 28, are now 24% off.

Before “cloud” was associated with On’s trainers and Phil Knight cofounded Blue Ribbon Sports, which eventually became Nike, there was Asics. The brand was founded over 75 years ago as Onitsuka Tiger, and would eventually merge with the Asics Corporation in 1977. The Asics “tiger stripes” logo on its shoes derives from the 1950s Onitsuka Tiger Mexico 66 shoe model. Its Gel-Cumulus and Gel-Nimbus legacy models were released in 1999.

Though the company is Japanese, the origin of Asics’s name is actually a Latin acronym, anima sana in corpore sano, for “sound mind in a sound body.” This ethos is exemplified when wearing, running, and racing in an Asics shoe. The brand’s dynamic cushioning provides comfort and a responsive ride for all running experiences. Well-received by wear-testers, we’ve included Asics trainers in multiple buying guides, including Best Running Shoes and the 2026 Shoe Awards.

Runner’s World has offered running advice and gear recommendations since 1966. We assembled a 300-plus-runner local group of varying experience levels, paces, and foot types to test the latest shoe releases and give their honest assessments on fit, comfort, and ride.

The shoes included on this list were all vetted by wear-testers and RW staff. I have also included my own experience testing some of these models during all kinds of workouts and in a couple of races.

RW contributor Michael Charboneau provided insight on Asics shoe tech and answered frequently asked questions about Asics trainers.

The Novablast 6 gets an injection of fun that is awfully reminiscent of the original. For this update, though, Asics cored out a hole in the forefoot and filled it with A-TPU, a foam that’s bouncier than PEBA. The effect is that the carrier (the bulk of the midsole) delivers a predictable, stable ride, yet the forefoot feels explosive and propulsive. It makes this everyday trainer suitable for days when you want to pick up the pace.

“The Asics Novablast 6 is a bouncy do-it-all shoe that excels with faster paces,” said tester and Runner’s World Editorial Assistant Michael McDonough. “Compared to other up-tempo daily trainers I’ve tested, like the. New Balance Rebel v5 and Nike Pegasus 42, it has more cushion and a softer feel, yet is still light and bouncier than both.”

Testers liked the reworked knit upper, improved AsicsGrip rubber outsole, and responsive trampoline pod of FF Turbo Squared foam in the forefoot.

“Cushioning is the strongest feature of this shoe,” said tester Trevor Conde. “The Novablast is a high-cushioned trainer and it delivers on that. The shoe has a bit more give than most of my go-to trainers, with a higher amount of sinking and compact cushioning during the foot strike phase.”

Shop Men’s at amazon.com | Shop Women’s at amazon.com

The GT-2000 underwent a makeover with its 14th iteration. Asics has carried these changes over to the GT-2000 15, ensuring the cushioning feels even softer with an added 2 mm of FF Blast Max foam. One tester said they had the same feel as the Hoka Clifton, saying the Asics shoe was just as comfortable.

The outsole has the same flame-like pods as the previous version for better traction and stability. The GT-2000 15 also has Asics’s 3D Guidance stability system, which involves high sidewalls for a secure fit and a wider platform for support.

“I’ve had the Asics GT-2000 13 and 14 models, and I was just has happy with this pair as I’ve been with the others,” said tester and overpronator Sophie Kahler. “I found it to be a solid sneaker for a beginner runner like myself who is looking for a mid-price, versatile shoe with good support. I tested it on road, treadmill, and gravel trail at my usual pace around 9:30 to 10:00. I also did a lot of walking in the shoes and found them comfortable for hours.”

For an even cheaper option, check out the GT-1000 14 ($115), which also has the brand’s 3D Guidance System.

Shop Men’s at amazon.com | Shop Women’s at amazon.com

The Gel-Cumulus is a long run favorite for its plush, supportive cushioning. It buffers miles of pounding in a surprisingly lightweight package. The shoe’s midsole is FF Blast Max, which promotes soft landings with high rebound. The foam—along with Asics’s PureGel tech—provides arch support for both neutral runners and underpronators.

“Compared to other daily trainers I have tested, the Asics Gel-Cumulus 28 is a perfect, stable, trainer,” said Caroline Lennon, a heel-striker who trains at 8:30 pace. “I found myself not interested in reaching for any other shoes in this period, no matter whether I was running on the treadmill, trail, or road. They were exceptionally comfortable and I never had any pain, discomfort, or nagging injury crop up in my time with these shoes.

“They don’t feel flashy, light, responsive and fast,” she continued. “But when I was waking up, and bleary-eyed pulling on my sneakers for a pre-dawn run, they felt like the comforting warm hug my feet wanted. Like getting back into bed. The cold streets/sidewalks didn’t feel nearly as jarring underfoot, and despite my feeling slow, I actually ran faster than I was expecting every time I wore these.”

Shop Men’s at amazon.com | Shop Women’s at amazon.com

Since its release 27 years ago, the Gel-Nimbus has delivered a premium cushioned, long-lasting ride. The Gel-Nimbus 28 is updated with 20 grams shaved off its weight, a feature testers were keyed in on when they ran in the shoe.

“I really like having a lightweight shoe that offers enough support for mostly road surface miles,” said Courtney Kazmierczak, an intermediate runner who trains at 9:15 pace with a forefoot strike. “The shoe feels like a feather when you hold it and honestly, putting it on I was doubtful that it would have enough cushion based on the weight of the shoe.” Kazmierczak shared that she had recent heel pain before testing the shoe and was surprised her runs were absent of discomfort in that area.

The Gel-Nimbus 28 has a much softer version of the brand’s PureGel tech in the midsole. The Gel tech combined with FF Blast Plus foam results in high energy return workouts and support that lasts for miles.

“The forefoot cushioning, like I mentioned in the overall rating. It was spot on,” said fellow forefoot striker Dave Brattley, who runs at 10:00 pace. “I’m still able to feel the road while still minimizing the impact. It made these shoes a real pleasure to run in.”

Shop Men’s at amazon.com | Shop Women’s at amazon.com

Year after year, the Gel-Kayano lands on our list of the best stability shoes for its comfortable fit and smooth ride. The latest version introduces Asics’s new stability tech: FluidSupport.

Replacing the 4D Guidance System, which made the shoe feel stiff, FluidSupport enhances cushioning with a dual layer of foam. FF Blast Plus and FF Blast Max are combined in the midsole; what you get is a softer top layer of foam and a denser bottom layer. Working in tandem with the shoe’s geometry, FluidSupport provides guidance only when you need it.

The result is a more flexible trainer that delivers high energy return on your runs.

Shop Men’s at amazon.com | Shop Women’s at amazon.com

The Magic Speed 5 is the cheaper but still capable carbon-fiber-plated racing shoe for the first-time marathoner or 26.2 vet looking for a speedwork trainer. FF Blast Plus foam cushions your landings along with a layer of the brand’s lightest and bounciest FF Leap foam. Asics also reduced the offset to 7mm and the heel height and forefoot height for a more stable ride.

Testers felt the shoe was too firm for long runs, but liked its responsiveness for shorter efforts during their training. Midfoot striker Gabrielle Kelenyi, who trains at 7:45 pace, said the Magic Speed 5 wouldn’t be her first choice of shoe in terms of comfort (the arch felt too pronounced for her foot), but the functionality was there.

“Without extra effort, I was going 15 to 30 seconds faster per mile on my runs,” she said. “These shoes offered good control during wet runs and up and down small hills. The lace closure was secure. Overall, I wore these for shorter runs (6 miles) and they gave those runs some extra oomph. They were not comfortable enough for longer runs (8+ miles).”

Other testers, like Stephanie Petrides, appreciated the arch support and overall cushioning.

“I have very flat feet and tend to give my knees and ankles a good pounding because of it, but the cushioning made everything very comfortable,” said Petrides, an overpronator. “The shoe was definitely not too soft and didn’t make me feel like it was slowing me down.”

I raced in the Metaspeed Edge Tokyo at the 2025 Sydney Marathon and didn’t expect to run 3:05 after combatting a week of being a tourist and jet lag. The shoe is more aggressive than the Metaspeed Edge Paris. Its bounce derives from a new layer of FF Leap foam, which is super light and responsive. The carbon plate is sandwiched between this top layer of Leap and FF Turbo Plus.

The Edge is made for cadence runners, with the plate at a lower angle in the forefoot area compared to the Metaspeed Sky Tokyo, which has a more equal distribution of foam with its carbon plate placement. We highlighted the Edge version here, but both models are favored by testers and can be worn by the same runner (some prefer the Sky for long races and the Edge for shorter races, like 5Ks, and vice versa).

“I think that the Metaspeeds are my all time favorite super shoe,” said tester Anthony Calantoni. “I have worn over 10 different pairs at this point and still find these to be the best feeling all around. They have definitely made improvements from the first edition which feel great.

“I think the increased padding on your foot is the biggest improvement from previous models. The old shoe you could feel the plate and the hardness was real, especially in a marathon. These have definitely improved in that area and you can feel it in most steps. I think I also love it because it still feels like a normal shoe but just with some enhancement of the speed.”

The Sonicblast is your prep shoe before showtime, or that trainer with just a little more oomph when you want to push the pace during workouts. A Pebax Astroplate is sandwiched between 46mm of FF Blast Max and FF Turbo Squared foams, to stabilize the ride as the shoe propels you forward. FF Turbo Squared is Asics’s high-performance A-TPU foam, which delivers aggressive rebound.

Testers loved the bouncy, high energy return ride and praised the shoe’s supportive cushioning.

“The best part of the shoe was the ride of the shoe for me,” said tester Tegan Kovacs, who’s been using the Sonicblast 2 for structured long runs. “It was very comfortable and honestly just plain fun! The shoe was comfortable and foamy enough to take on longer distances, and delivered a propulsive ride when you kicked it up a notch.”

While testers like the Sonicblast 2’s propulsive ride, some were wary of sharp corners due to the shoe’s tall stack height.

“I found that taking a turn does require a little more care to counter some of the instability of the higher stack height, but it wasn’t enough of a concern for me to worry too much about it,” said editor Ashley Tysiac. “Because the cushioning is much more firm rather than plush, I could still easily navigate a fork in the road or a turn on the greenway without feeling like I was going to turn my ankle.”

Shop Men’s at amazon.com | Shop Women’s at amazon.com

The Blast series hits the trail. Testers loved the comfort the Blazeblast provided fit-wise and on the run. The shoe has FF Blast Max cushioning to provide a plush, high-energy-return ride. The trampoline pod outsole and midsole design promotes propulsion during toe-off.

The AsicsGrip outsole was satisfactory for our testers who ran the shoe on the road, towpaths, and semi-rocky terrain.

“The only shoe that I can kind of compare this to were the Hoka Mafate Speed 4,” said tester Anna Piskorska. “Both of them are very light and have a great flexibility at the midfoot. The Asics give you enough cushion throughout the foot. There’s a noticeable bounce feeling, which allows you to quickly lift off and pick up speed instantly.”

Some testers wanted longer lugs for dicier trail efforts. “For a shoe with trail running as a mission, the tread is a bit lacking with the 2.5mm lugs as they will serve you well on mild inclines but anything wet or steep (or wet and steep!) is likely going to be troublesome,” said tester Eric Bartosz. “Just like my Kawasaki, it’s fine for some easy trails, but I would need to change tires for anything more demanding or technical...and that’s OK!”

Still, testers appreciated how the Blazeblast made runs feel easier and faster off road.

Shop Men’s at asics.com | Shop Women’s at asics.com

The Megablast has that high-octane, pogo stick bounce that makes it earn our Most Aggressive title. The shoe’s midsole is pure FF Turbo Squared, Asics’s bounciest foam. At a tall 46mm stack height, the Megablast is a lot of shoe at a surprisingly light weight.

Josh Davis, an underpronator who trains at 7:00 pace, described the shoe as bulky but appreciated its bouncy ride.

“This is a pretty darn good shoe,” he said. “The super high deck broadcasts the FF Turbo Squared foam, and it lives up to its name. For its size, the shoe is pretty darn light and very responsive. I’ve put over 100 miles on it at this point, and haven’t noticed any change in the pop. I liked this shoe for easy runs. I didn’t try to push it in any workouts because the shoe was a bit bulky.”

Some testers, including myself, felt the ride was too squishy and erratic in a whole lot of shoe. RW contributor and tester Heather Mayer Irvine said “the junk in the trunk” was her least favorite aspect of the Megablast.

With the Superblast 3 you get the best of both worlds in terms of cushioning and ride. The midsole has FF Blast Plus foam and FF Leap on a trampoline pod-shaped sole, designed to encourage better toe-off.

Runners loved its soft but supportive foam and bounce. Said intermediate runner and 7:45 pacer Erin Dewalt: “I like the combination of lightweight cushion and bounce most. For half marathon and marathon training, when you’re logging lots of miles, foot comfort is paramount. During my long runs, I’d marvel at how comfortable my feet felt even towards the end.”

Nick Miller, an underpronator and heel striker, named the cushioning as his favorite Superblast 3 feature.

“The cushioning of the Superblast 3 is what truly sets it apart from other shoes I’ve tested,” he said. “Its substantial stack height provides exceptional impact absorption, noticeably reducing the stress on my legs during runs. This made a clear difference on longer efforts, where fatigue typically builds up, and allows me to recover more quickly between sessions.”

Some testers, however, including myself, felt the loudness of the shoe was distracting. When I tested the Superblast 3 on my runs, the pavement slapping was comparable to Nike’s Alphaflys.

Asics has cooked up quite a few proprietary features, and you’ll see many different terms when browsing the company’s running shoe lineup. To help you get more insight into these features, compare models, and find the right shoe, here’s a deeper dive on the main Asics running shoe tech to know.

This tech consists of a squishy, gel-like substance implanted in the midsole, and it absorbs impact forces for a smoother ride. The latest iteration is PureGel, and it’s formulated to be lighter, softer, and more flexible than previous versions of Gel.

Like other shoemakers, Asics has its own proprietary cushioning, called FlyteFoam (FF). Although it’s based on ethylene-vinyl acetate (EVA), the traditional running shoe cushioning material, this foam is formulated to be lighter and more resilient than standard EVA. It doesn’t have quite the same springy feel as the other types of FF below, but it works fine for everyday running. It’s used in Asics’s more affordable shoes.

FF Blast Plus is the next level up. Asics hasn’t released details on the chemistry, but it likely includes olefin block copolymers, which make for a lighter, more flexible and more responsive foam. For a pillowy and springy ride that still holds up to everyday training, FF Blast Plus is the cushioning to go with.

Asics has also released an updated version, called FF Blast Max, that has a lower density, so it’s even softer and bouncier. It gives models a very plush ride. For maximum cushioning that doesn’t sacrifice responsiveness, look for training shoes with FF Blast Max.

Asics’s elite racing shoes have FF Turbo Plus foam. It’s made with polyether block amide (PEBA), an exceptionally light, soft, and bouncy material. The brand took this foam up a notch with the even bouncier FF Turbo Squared. Leap foam, which is made of Aliphatic TPU (A-TPU), is a super foam that’s softer and lighter than FF Turbo Squares. It is used in the brand’s top tier racing shoes. The shoes with this type of cushioning are pricey, but provide excellent shock absorption and springy responsiveness for a smooth, propulsive ride that helps you go fast. For race day, it’s definitely the top choice.

Asics takes a holistic approach to stability in its shoes, with several features working together to support the foot and guide it from landing to toe-off. The latest version of its stability feature-set is called the “4D Guidance System.” The 4D Guidance shoes feature a wide sole, a firm foam layer in midsole under the arch, and a flared sole shape at the heel to create a planted feel while counteracting overpronation, or excessive inward rolling motion in your step.

Some models have an earlier version of the system, called 3D Guidance. It has the same general features as 4D, but lacks the firm arch support foam in the midsole. If you know you need stability shoes, or simply prefer a more guided, supportive design, then you should look for these features.

Asics has developed a well-deserved reputation for manufacturing reliable shoes that can hold up through high-mileage training. Core models like the Gel-Cumulus, Gel-Nimbus, and Gel-Kayano have been around for decades (and continuously improved upon in that time), and they’re great picks if you’re looking for everyday trainers.

That said, the brand has also expanded into lightweight, responsive racing shoes and even trail shoes, too.

How do Asics shoes compare to shoes from other brands?

Historically, Asics shoes have been known for using multiple layers of cushioning to create a stable, well-cushioned (and somewhat stiff) ride. Core models like the Gel-Cumulus still exhibit this construction, with a moderate drop and layers of Gel and foam in the midsole for a plush feel that’s great for long runs and training miles.

However, newer shoes in the Asics lineup, like the Novablast, utilize more lightweight, bouncy midsole designs that mirror what other top brands are doing in their premium speedwork and racing shoes.

Has Asics created any key innovations in running shoe tech?

The short answer: Yes, lots of them. Asics has been experimenting with running shoe tech for well over half a century. In 1990, the brand opened the Institute of Sports Science in Kobe, Japan, where the company conducts materials tests and biomechanical research to fine-tune designs.

This lab has produced and refined many of Asics’s hallmark technologies, like Gel cushioning and super foams, like FF Leap and FF Turbo Squared. For runners, this means Asics shoes are built with proven designs that can help you meet your goals, from sticking to a training plan to nabbing a new PR on race day.

Amanda Furrer, Editor, Running Reviews, studied journalism at NYU and writing at Emerson College. She has reviewed gear and covered other topics in the running space for almost 10 years. Since 2013, she has consecutively run the Boston Marathon. She also has a master’s degree in gastronomy from Boston University and was formerly a professional baker for two years before hanging up her apron.

The ultimate domestic travel rewards benefit for families and couples

Imagine this: you book a flight for yourself, and your spouse — or your best friend, or your mom — flies with you for the cost of taxes alone. Not a discount. Not a sale. Completely. Free. For up to two full calendar years. That's the Southwest Companion Pass, and it is, without question, the single most powerful perk in all of domestic travel rewards. The ChooseFI community has a saying: if you only ever pursue one travel rewards strategy in your life, make it this one. Here's the math that makes your jaw drop. A round-trip Southwest flight from Denver to Cancún might run $400 per person. A family of four flying during spring break? You're looking at $1,600 cash. But with the Companion Pass, you pay for two tickets and the other two fly nearly free (taxes and fees only) — cutting your out-of-pocket cost in half, every single flight, for nearly two years. Run the numbers over a year of typical family travel and you're looking at **$2,000 to $8,000 in total value** from a single benefit. The CPP (cents per point) range here — **1.5 to 5.9 cents per point** — is what makes this genuinely remarkable. Southwest's Rapid Rewards program values points at roughly 1.4 cents toward any flight. But the Companion Pass doesn't just redeem points efficiently; it *doubles the value of every redemption you make while it's active*. That's the pricing inefficiency the loyalty system has quietly built in, and the FI community is uniquely positioned to exploit it. Think about what 135,000 points normally buys: roughly $1,890 worth of Southwest flights. Solid, but not earth-shattering. Now attach the Companion Pass, and those same points — redeemed strategically over two years — effectively unlock $3,780 or more in flight value for your household. No blackout dates. No seat restrictions. No change fees. Just book, fly, repeat. This isn't a first-class lounge or a lie-flat bed over the Pacific. It's something arguably more valuable for the FI-minded family: **sustainable, repeatable, nearly free domestic travel** that works with your actual life.

The Companion Pass isn't a points redemption — it's a status benefit. That distinction is everything, and it's the insight that separates people who get this from people who miss it entirely.

Here's how it works: Southwest grants the Companion Pass when you earn 135,000 qualifying Rapid Rewards points in a single calendar year. Once you hit that threshold, you designate one person as your companion, and that person flies with you on every flight — paid or points — for the remainder of that calendar year plus the entire following calendar year.

The key word is "earn." Points transferred in from partners count. Credit card signup bonuses count. Shopping portal purchases count. Almost every way you accumulate points counts toward the 135,000 threshold — except points purchased directly from Southwest.

The pricing inefficiency here is a calendar arbitrage opportunity. If you earn the Companion Pass on January 2nd, you get it for the rest of that year and all of the next year — nearly two full calendar years of 2-for-1 flights. If you earn it on November 15th, you get roughly 13 months. The strategy is to time your credit card signup bonuses to post in January, maximizing your benefit window.

Most ChooseFI members build their 135,000 points through a combination of strategies:

Chase Ultimate Rewards → Southwest Rapid Rewards (1:1, Instant) Chase transfers to Southwest at a 1:1 ratio and the transfer is instant — points appear in your Rapid Rewards account within minutes. This makes Chase points (earned on cards like the Chase Sapphire Preferred or Ink Business cards) the most efficient fuel for this strategy.

Marriott Bonvoy® → Southwest Rapid Rewards (3:1, 1-5 days) Marriott transfers at a 3:1 ratio (3 Marriott points = 1 Southwest point), and transfers take 1-5 days. This is a less efficient path — use it only if you have a surplus of Marriott points and no better option.

The most reliable path to 135,000 points is stacking Southwest credit card signup bonuses. Southwest's consumer and business cards frequently offer bonuses of 50,000-75,000 points each. A couple who each opens one card, or one person who opens both a personal and business card, can often hit the threshold with signup bonuses alone — before spending a dollar on the portal.

Since Southwest charges no fuel surcharges on award flights and points never expire, there's no penalty for building this balance over several months. The Rapid Rewards program is revenue-based with dynamic pricing, meaning points cover the full fare including taxes — no hidden redemption fees to erode your value.

Log into your Chase Ultimate Rewards account and your Southwest Rapid Rewards account and tally your existing points. You need 135,000 qualifying Rapid Rewards points earned in a single calendar year to trigger the Companion Pass. Note: points already sitting in your Rapid Rewards account from prior years don't count — you need to earn 135,000 in the target calendar year.

The optimal window is October through December of the prior year. Apply for Southwest credit cards (personal and/or business) so that your signup bonuses post to your Rapid Rewards account in January. Verify with Southwest's current card offers — signup bonuses of 50,000-75,000 points are common. A couple can each apply for a card; a solo pursuer can apply for both a personal and a business card if they have qualifying self-employment income.

Call Chase or Southwest after your first statement closes to confirm when points will post. Timing is everything.

Once your signup bonuses post, calculate how many points you still need. If you're short:

Southwest will notify you by email once you've crossed 135,000 qualifying points. Log into your Rapid Rewards account at southwest.com and navigate to "My Account" → "Companion Pass" to confirm the benefit is active.

You can designate — and change — your companion up to three times per calendar year. Name your most frequent travel partner first. Go to southwest.com, log in, and find the Companion Pass section to add their name and contact information.

Searching is simple: go to southwest.com and search any route. Toggle between "$ Dollars" and "Rapid Rewards Points" to see your cost. When you book with points and your companion is designated, Southwest will automatically prompt you to add your companion to the same flight. Your companion pays taxes only — typically $5.60 each way for domestic flights.

Pro tip: Southwest opens its booking window 330 days in advance. For peak travel like spring break or holiday weeks, set a calendar reminder and book the day the window opens.

The Companion Pass works because Southwest treats it as a status benefit rather than a points redemption. Most airline companion programs require you to burn miles for the second ticket or limit usage to specific fare classes. Southwest flips this model: once you earn the pass, your companion flies on every single flight you take — paid or award — for the remainder of the qualifying year plus the entire following calendar year. The only cost is taxes. Because Southwest has no blackout dates, no fuel surcharges, and no change fees, the pass amplifies in value with every trip you take. The January-earning calendar arbitrage is the key optimization that turns a good benefit into an extraordinary one.

Let's make this real. It's March, and your family of four wants to spend a week in Orlando this July — theme parks, pool time, the works.

A quick search on southwest.com shows round-trip flights from Chicago Midway to Orlando for $320 per person. For four tickets, that's $1,280 cash. Standard family travel math: painful but doable.

You have the Companion Pass active, earned back in January. You book two tickets: yours at 22,000 Rapid Rewards points (worth ~$308 at 1.4 cents per point), and your spouse's ticket at $5.60 in taxes as your designated companion. Your two kids? You use 44,000 more points for their tickets. Total out-of-pocket: 66,000 points + $11.20 in taxes.

Let's value those 66,000 points at their Chase transfer cost — you transferred them 1:1 from Chase Ultimate Rewards, where they were worth roughly $825 in travel via the portal. But by pairing them with the Companion Pass, your spouse flies nearly free, effectively doubling your points' purchasing power on this trip.

Cash price: $1,280. Your cost: 66,000 points + $11.20. That's a CPP of roughly 1.9 cents per point on the base redemption — but accounting for your companion flying nearly free, the effective CPP on the entire trip rockets to 3.8 cents per point. Well within the 1.5–5.9 cent range where this sweet spot lives.

And here's what makes Southwest specifically wonderful for families: no change fees. Book in March, change in June when your kid's baseball tournament schedule shifts, rebook without penalty. No one in the FI community is paying $200-per-person change fees.

The experience itself? Economy class on Southwest, open seating, snacks, and friendly crew. It's not lie-flat business class to Tokyo — but that's not the point. The point is your family of four flies to Florida for a week, and the flights barely register on your annual budget. That's FI-level travel.

Time your credit card applications so signup bonuses post in January of your target year. A bonus that posts January 5th gives you until December 31st of the following year to use the Companion Pass — nearly 24 months of 2-for-1 flights. This single timing decision can mean the difference between 13 months and 23 months of value.

The Rapid Rewards Shopping Portal (rapidrewardsshopping.com) awards points on purchases at hundreds of retailers. Even after you've earned the Companion Pass, continuing to earn Rapid Rewards points means more flights at lower point costs. Treat it like a cashback portal and check it before any online purchase.

Southwest opens availability 330 days in advance. For Thanksgiving, Christmas, spring break, and summer weekends in popular markets, set a calendar reminder and book the exact morning the window opens. Southwest doesn't have blackout dates, but high-demand flights sell out in Wanna Get Away fare class — the cheapest points tier — quickly.

You can change your designated companion up to three times per calendar year. If your life situation changes — a different travel partner, a new relationship, a child aging into a separate ticket — use this flexibility. Just don't burn all three changes frivolously.

Purchased points do not count toward the 135,000 qualifying threshold for the Companion Pass. Don't make this mistake when you're close to the threshold — transfer from Chase instead.

Some people try to earn the Companion Pass in November or December. You'll get it for only a few weeks before the calendar resets. The math simply doesn't work. January earning is the only strategy worth pursuing.

The Southwest Rapid Rewards Performance Business Credit Card (or similar business cards) have separate signup bonuses that stack with personal card bonuses. If you have any self-employment income — freelancing, a side hustle, a rental property — you likely qualify. This is often the fastest path to 135,000 points for a single applicant.

The Southwest Companion Pass was practically invented for the FI-minded family. If you have a consistent travel partner — a spouse, a partner, a parent you visit annually — and you fly domestically more than two or three times a year, this benefit will transform your travel budget.

Minimum points to get started: You need to earn 135,000 qualifying Rapid Rewards points in a single calendar year. In practice, this means you either need access to Southwest credit card signup bonuses (which requires good to excellent credit, typically 700+) or a substantial existing balance of Chase Ultimate Rewards points to transfer at 1:1.

How it fits the FI strategy: The Companion Pass is a force multiplier. Every dollar you would have spent on a second ticket stays in your investment accounts instead. Over a two-year Companion Pass window, a couple who takes six domestic trips per year could easily bank $2,000-$4,000 in travel savings — real money that compounds.

Who this is NOT for: Solo travelers get zero benefit from the Companion Pass. International travelers who primarily fly non-Southwest routes won't find much use here. And if you're averse to economy class or require a specific airline's premium cabin, this redemption isn't your path.

The Southwest Companion Pass earns a **moderate difficulty rating** — and that rating is almost entirely about the *earning*, not the booking. Once you have the Companion Pass, booking is literally the simplest award experience in travel rewards: search southwest.com, find your flight, click "Add Companion." There are no partner airlines to navigate, no availability calendars to decode, no call centers to endure. It's a 5/5 on ease of booking for a reason. The moderate rating comes from **three earning challenges**: **1. The credit requirement.** Southwest credit cards require good to excellent credit. If you're early in your credit-building journey, this strategy may need to wait 12-18 months while you strengthen your profile. **2. The timing discipline.** Earning the pass is straightforward, but earning it in January takes planning. You need to apply for cards 2-3 months in advance and coordinate signup bonus posting dates — something most people have never had to think about. **3. The 135,000-point threshold.** This is a real number. It requires intentional credit card strategy, not casual spending. For a single applicant without a business card, it may require supplementing with Chase transfers or portal activity. **How to overcome these challenges:** - Start planning in **October or November** for a January earn target - Check whether you qualify for a Southwest business card — it dramatically simplifies reaching the threshold - Use the Rapid Rewards Shopping Portal year-round to passively accumulate qualifying points If you've successfully applied for a travel rewards credit card before and you have a consistent travel partner, you can absolutely do this. The ChooseFI community has helped hundreds of families earn the Companion Pass — and not one of them regretted the effort.

Open a personal and/or business Southwest credit card so that signup bonuses of 50,000 to 75,000 points each will post to your Rapid Rewards account in January. Call to confirm when points will post after your first statement closes.

Once signup bonuses post, calculate your gap. Transfer Chase Ultimate Rewards at 1:1 (instant) to fill any shortfall. Use the Rapid Rewards Shopping Portal for additional earning on everyday purchases.

After Southwest confirms your Companion Pass, log in to southwest.com and designate your travel partner. Book flights as normal — Southwest will prompt you to add your companion for taxes only ($5.60 each way domestic).

Set calendar reminders for Thanksgiving, Christmas, spring break, and summer travel. Southwest opens its booking window 330 days in advance. Book the morning the window opens to lock in Wanna Get Away fares at the lowest point costs.

This is why timing your earning to January is the critical optimization.

The Southwest Companion Pass is the single most powerful domestic travel rewards benefit available to FI-minded families and couples. At a cost of 135,000 qualifying points — achievable through credit card signup bonuses and Chase transfers — you unlock nearly two full years of 2-for-1 flights on every Southwest route with no blackout dates and no change fees. A family of four taking six domestic trips per year can realistically save $2,000 to $4,000 annually, money that goes straight back into your investment accounts. Time your earning to January, stack your signup bonuses, and designate your most frequent travel partner. This is the redemption that makes domestic travel a rounding error in your FI budget.

#8603. The Best Protein Powders for Weight Loss, According to a Certified Nutrition Coach

Protein powder can help you maintain muscle mass while eating in a calorie deficit. We tested more than 100 protein powders and found nine we think are best for weight loss.

Written by Stephen Sheehan, CPT × The Expert Panel is a network of specialized health and fitness professionals who help ensure we present the most accurate information to our readers. This includes physicians, certified trainers, elite-level coaches, and more. Learn more about our experts. expert-verified Amanda Dvorak, ISSA-CPT, ISSA-CNC Last updated on Feb 19, 2025

expert-verified Amanda Dvorak, ISSA-CPT, ISSA-CNC

When someone says they want to lose weight, what they really mean is they want to shed excess body fat. However, without a well-designed plan in place, a calorie deficit leads you to lose both fat and valuable muscle tissue. To minimize muscle loss, it’s crucial to incorporate resistance training, quality sleep, and a high-protein diet into your regular routine.

Protein plays a multifaceted role in weight management, influencing factors like hunger levels, metabolism, and muscle preservation. While heavy resistance training provides the necessary stimulus, signaling to the body that existing muscle should be retained, a high-protein diet ensures the body has an ample supply of amino acids. This prevents your body from metabolizing muscle tissue for energy.

The best protein powders provide a convenient and lean source of the muscle-building macronutrient, helping you hit your daily protein goals while also maintaining a calorie deficit. We tested more than 100 protein powders and selected nine products we think are best for weight loss.

This content is meant to be informative, but should not be taken as medical advice. It is not intended for use as diagnosis, prevention, or treatment of health problems. Always speak with your doctor before starting any new supplement or exercise regimen.

We chose these products based on a number of factors, including:

I chose Transparent Labs as the best protein powder for weight loss because it has a very high ratio of protein to the total number of calories: 28 grams to 130 calories. This helps you maximize protein consumption during a caloric deficit, which helps prevent you from losing muscle while you’re losing weight. It’s also third-party tested, Informed Choice certified, and completely artificial ingredient-free. And it comes in 15 flavor options.

I’ve tried a number of different flavors from Transparent Labs and Chocolate Peanut Butter is by far my favorite, followed closely by Mocha. I found they mixed easily in both a blender and a conventional shaker bottle. Whenever I’m trying to cut weight, I find this delicious protein powder helps curb my sweet tooth and tide me over between meals.

While I didn’t personally experience this, some customer reviews mention it can be challenging to get in contact with Transparent Labs’ customer service team.

Jacked Factory Authentic Iso has 25 grams of protein per serving, 2 grams of carbohydrates, and just 0.5 grams of fat, which is the least amount of fat of any powder on our list. If you’re looking to lose weight, this macronutrient profile will help keep you on the right track. However, something to keep in mind: This protein powder is sweetened with sucralose, which is an artificial sweetener—studies link these sweeteners to increased cancer risk. Additionally, unlike most brands on our list, Jacked Factory doesn’t do third-party testing on its products. This means there isn’t a guarantee the ingredients are pure and match the ingredient label.

Kessler tried Jacked Factory Authentic Iso and was impressed. “This is the only protein powder I’ve tried that didn’t settle at all,” he says. “I found it a bit too sweet, but if you’re looking for a powder that tastes like dessert, you should opt for this one.”

If you’re looking for one of the best vegan protein powders that also works with a weight loss diet, Ka’Chava is a great choice. This vegan protein powder is marketed as a “whole-body meal,” which means it’s designed as a meal replacement rather than an addition to a meal or snack, like the other protein powders on our list. That’s why the calorie, carbohydrate, and fat counts (240, 25 grams, and 7 grams, respectively), are higher. The carb count is high for those on a low-carb diet, so that’s something to look out for. However, it packs in 25 grams of plant protein, derived from a combination of peas, brown rice, and quinoa, which will help preserve muscle while on a weight loss diet.

Tester Zoe Ettinger, a C.N.C.-in-training, uses this protein powder often. “I’m a big fan of Ka’Chava. It tastes delicious mixed in a smoothie with some frozen blueberries,” she says. “I also like that it also has adaptogens, probiotics, greens, and probiotics. I notice a difference in how good I feel when I take Ka’Chava regularly,” she says.

One thing to note about Ka’Chava is that it is the most expensive option on our list at $79.99 for a 15-serving bag. While the price reflects the fact that this protein powder is intended as a meal replacement, it’s still a big investment.

I chose Nutricost as the best protein powder for weight loss available on Amazon because its calorie and macronutrient profile is ideal for shedding pounds. Nutricost has a high protein content per serving, which is important for weight loss as protein can help enhance satiety and preserve muscle mass while in a deficit. With minimal fat and carbohydrates, this protein ensures you get the maximum protein intake without the added calories, making it an ideal choice for those looking to lose weight efficiently.

The taste and mixability of this protein are also top-notch. I tested the Vanilla flavor; it blended excellently in both milk and water and had an authentic vanilla taste profile. Despite using artificial sweeteners, which often make products sickly sweet, I found the sweetness level to be on point. However, if you’re trying to avoid artificial sweeteners, choose Promix or Transparent Labs, which use natural sweeteners.

Huel is our favorite meal replacement for weight loss because it has a great protein-to-carb ratio. Huel has 40 grams of protein per serving, the most of any protein powder on our list, and 24 grams of carbs. While this might be more carbs than ideal for those on a keto diet, it’s a solid portion for most. Carbs are an essential nutrient and according to experts, you can consume 100 to 150 grams a day and still lose weight.

Kessler tried Huel in Chocolate and Vanilla. “The Chocolate flavor was great, probably because it uses real cocoa powder, which gave it an authentic chocolate flavor,” he says. “The Vanilla wasn’t as good—it didn’t really taste like vanilla and had an artificial aftertaste.” He notes that it doesn’t mix very well, but says it made him feel great. “Other similar products, like Transparent Labs Mass Gainer, give me an upset stomach. But I felt great after taking Huel Black Edition,” he says.

Promix is our favorite clean protein powder because it’s third-party tested and results are easily viewable on Promix’s website. Those results show this product is tested for heavy metals and verified gluten-free. And beyond these positive results, this protein powder has one of the most simple formulas on our list. Vanilla, for example, has just four ingredients, and Promix doesn’t use any artificial ingredients.

This protein powder, like others on our list, has a solid protein-to-carb ratio for weight loss (25 grams to 7 grams, respectively). A 2020 study found consuming a higher portion of protein versus carbs helped participants lose weight and prevented them from gaining the weight back.

I tried the Vanilla flavor of this protein powder. I enjoyed it for the most part, but it wasn’t quite sweet enough for my taste. And I wish it mixed a little better—there were some clumps after mixing.

One thing to note about Promix is that while it has been third-party tested, it hasn’t been third-party tested for sport specifically. This means it hasn’t been tested for substances banned in athletic competitions. So if you’re an athlete planning to compete, opt for a powder that’s Informed Sport Certified or NSF Certified for Sport.

One of my favorite casein protein powders is Casein+ from Legion Athletics. I chose Casein+ because it’s all-natural, meaning it’s free from artificial sweeteners, flavors, and colors, and it’s third-party tested by Labdoor for purity and potency. This product provides 25 grams of protein per serving and only contains 110 calories, regardless of the flavor you choose. This protein-to-calorie ratio is ideal for weight loss.

Along with whey, casein is a type of protein found in milk and is characterized by its slow digestion and absorption. This prolonged digestion makes it an ideal option for people looking to manage hunger levels and maintain a consistent supply of amino acids over an extended timeframe—such as during sleep or when going a long time between meals. By providing a steady stream of protein to the muscles, casein helps mitigate the risk of muscle breakdown that often accompanies calorie restriction. As a result, incorporating a casein protein powder into your diet can be a strategic move to help support your weight loss goals.

Tester Brandon Lunsford, C.P.T., tried the Dutch Chocolate flavor, saying it reminded him of a dark chocolate bar that isn’t too rich or too sweet. The only downside is that casein protein has a different consistency than whey. It’s generally thicker and often takes longer to dissolve. Lunsford noticed this during his testing, saying the product had a “slightly chalky aftertaste.”

Naked Whey’s Unflavored protein stands out for its simplicity and purity; its single-ingredient formula consists of whey protein concentrate sourced for grass-fed cows. This simplicity aligns with the brand’s commitment to transparency, priding itself on avoiding additives, fillers, or artificial ingredients in its products.

With its neutral taste profile, this protein powder is very versatile, letting you integrate the protein powder seamlessly into your favorite recipes or smoothies without altering the flavor profile. Kessler tried the Unflavored version and says it “has a very slight vanilla taste to it.” He also detected a note of earthiness, but says “It would be really good mixed into a smoothie.” However, he mentions the two-scoop serving size can feel like a lot, so he recommends using extra liquid when blending it.

If you’re someone who prefers a flavored protein powder, you’ll be happy to know Naked also offers five flavored options, including Chocolate, Vanilla, Strawberry, Chocolate Peanut Butter, and Double Chocolate. Naked only uses coconut sugar to sweeten its protein supplements, which isn’t nearly as sweet as artificial sweeteners like sucralose or acesulfame potassium.

We chose Sports Research as our best protein powder for weight loss and muscle gain because it has a solid protein-to-calorie ratio (25 grams to 140 calories), is Informed Sport Certified, is fairly priced at $1.20 per serving, and tastes great, according to testers.

From a nutritional standpoint, Sports Research stacks up well against many of its competitors. The per-serving content for protein (25 grams), calories (140), and carbs (2 grams) compares favorably with most of the choices on our list, although the fat per serving (3.5 grams for Vanilla and 4 grams for Dutch Chocolate) is on the high side. Other ingredients include vitamin D, which has been linked to muscle health in recent research.

Tester Cory Kessler, C.N.C., C.P.T., tried the Creamy Vanilla flavor. “When I mixed it with milk it almost tasted like vanilla ice cream,” he says. “But when I mixed it with water it diluted the flavor, and all I could taste was the sweetness,” he warns. He also notes that it mixed very well, and “wasn’t gritty or clumpy at all.”

Whether from powder or whole food sources, protein aids weight loss mainly by:

Protein powder can be an effective tool in helping you achieve your weight loss goals. Drinking a protein powder shake or smoothie provides a quick, easy way to consume high amounts of protein with a limited amount of calories, fat, and carbohydrates. One of the main benefits of protein powder is that it’s often extremely lean, with a very high ratio of protein to total number of calories. This makes protein powder an efficient way to hit your daily protein target while adhering to your calorie guidelines.

Choose a protein powder with a significant amount of protein, typically around 25 grams per serving. If you have weight loss goals, a whey, soy, or pea protein isolate is likely your best bet since they are ultra-filtered to remove excess carbohydrates and fats.

When you have weight loss goals, it’s best to choose a protein powder with a moderate calorie count per serving, e.g., 100 to 160 calories. You should also ensure the majority of those calories come from protein, as this will best support your weight loss progress. Remember, protein is four calories per gram, so you can expect a supplement that has 25 grams of protein to have around 110 to 120 calories if it’s extremely lean.

It’s important to check the ingredients list of the supplement to ensure the product is free from added sugars or unnecessary fillers. Although these ingredients may contribute to the flavor, sweetness, and creaminess of the supplement, they often come with added calories. It’s generally best to select protein powders with minimal ingredients.

Occasionally, protein powders contain ingredients such as creatine, probiotics, or branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs). While these aren’t necessary, it’s important to assess whether these added ingredients align with your health and fitness goals, and whether it’s worth choosing a protein powder that offers these options.

Regardless of your goals, choose a protein powder with a flavor and consistency you enjoy. I know this seems obvious, but if you dislike the taste, then you’re far less likely to use the protein powder on a consistent basis, if at all.

As a certified nutrition coach, I advise my clients to choose a protein powder that’s been third-party tested for quality, purity, and safety, especially when I’m working with athletes. This ensures your supplement is free from contaminants, including banned substances, and is deemed safe for consumption. Third-party testing also holds supplement companies accountable, providing assurance that the ingredients in the product align with the information provided on the supplement facts label.

Whenever you’re purchasing a dietary supplement, you should look for one that aligns with your specific health and fitness goals. With weight loss in mind, it’s typically recommended to avoid products with added sugars, or excessive amounts of carbohydrates and fats. Some consumers may also choose to avoid products with artificial additives, such as sweeteners, flavors, and colors, which are routinely found in protein powder supplements. If you’re looking for an all-natural protein powder with minimal ingredients, consider Transparent Labs 100% Grass-Fed Whey or protein powders from Naked Nutrition.

As a certified nutrition coach, I think it’s important to emphasize that a protein powder isn’t a necessity for weight loss success. However, due to its convenience and effectiveness, it does offer some notable benefits when used as part of a holistic approach to weight loss that includes resistance training, quality sleep, and healthy lifestyle habits. Consuming a high-protein diet, especially during a weight-loss phase, helps manage hunger levels and improves muscle preservation. If a protein powder can help you hit your daily protein targets while still maintaining a calorie deficit, then I think it’s worth incorporating into your regular routine.

Protein shakes are an excellent way to help preserve lean muscle mass when pursuing your weight loss goals. If weight loss is your primary objective, I’d suggest opting for a whey protein isolate, such as Transparent Labs 100% Grass-Fed Whey. This protein powder is incredibly lean, meaning the majority of calories come from protein alone. This can help you achieve your daily protein targets without over-consuming calories from the additional carbohydrates and fats commonly found in a whey protein concentrate.

Weight loss strategies vary from person to person, however, individuals with weight loss goals should aim for at least 1.2 to 1.6 grams of protein per kilogram of body weight. (This equates to approximately 0.5 to 0.7 grams of protein per pound of body weight.) This range should provide enough protein to support muscle mass while maintaining a calorie deficit, which is necessary for weight loss.

With protein powder for weight loss, certain protein sources are considered “leaner” than others. For example, whey protein isolates benefit from various kinds of processing and filtration that lower the fat and carbohydrates in the finished product. The main drawback with some plant-based proteins is that they can be naturally higher in carbs. Fortunately, high-quality plant protein powders could deliver comparable results to whey protein in terms of promoting lean body mass.Lean animal proteins include chicken breast, fish, and eggs. Even certain cuts of beef (sirloin) and pork (loin) are considered lean. Greek yogurt, tofu, beans, and lentils are among the non-animal sources of lean protein.

When focusing on weight loss, it’s best to steer clear of calorie-rich beverages such as sugary sodas and sports drinks, fruit juices, and alcohol. Instead, choose options like water, seltzer, black coffee, and unsweetened tea, all of which are essentially calorie-free. Avoiding calorie-dense beverages allows you to allocate those calories to food instead, which should help improve your satiety or feelings of fullness after meals.

There’s no protein that targets belly fat loss specifically. However, prioritizing lean protein, such as a whey protein isolate, can be beneficial for your overall weight loss goals. Whey protein isolates are processed to minimize the carbohydrate and fat content, maximizing the protein-to-calorie ratio of the supplement. This makes them an efficient option to support your intake of dietary protein while maintaining a calorie deficit.

When he’s not creating content or hitting the gym, he enjoys traveling, cooking, and attending music festivals around the world.
